notes.meaning: Praising the Lord and singing to His name is both a duty and a deep joy. The heading marks this song for the Sabbath, showing that God's day of rest is especially meant for worship. Giving thanks is good because God deserves it, it lifts our hearts, and it encourages others to honor Him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that the true Sabbath rest is inside the believer's heart, where one enjoys a quiet, peaceful conscience before God.

notes.meaning: God's people are called to praise Him at the start and the close of every day. In the morning, we remember the loving care that protected us through the night and gave us a new day. At night, we look back and thank Him for faithfully keeping all His promises.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine understood morning to mean times of joy when we praise God's mercy, and night to mean times of trouble when we trust His justice and truth.

notes.meaning: Stringed instruments such as harps and lyres accompanied the singing of sacred songs in ancient Israel. These instruments brought beauty and dignity to worship, helping people quiet their thoughts and focus entirely on God.

differ.view: Some historically followed John Calvin in teaching that musical instruments belonged to Old Testament shadows and should not be used in Christian public worship.
Musical instruments are welcomed as fitting tools to accompany singing and enrich church praise.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine interpreted the ten strings allegorically as the Ten Commandments, and the harp as a picture of doing good works.

notes.meaning: Praise flows naturally from a heart that sees what God has accomplished. The writer rejoices not in his own skills, but in God's mighty acts of creation, care, and rescue. Meditating on what the Lord has done turns worship into genuine gladness.

God's deeds are vast and wonderful, and the plans behind them are deeper than any human mind can fathom. People can only see a small portion of how the Lord governs the world. Standing before His wisdom should fill us with humble awe.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine saw God's deep thoughts here as the mystery of why the wicked flourish and the good suffer, a mystery believers can bear only by holding fast to Christ's cross.

notes.meaning: A person who lives only by physical impulses cannot understand God's deeper ways. Such people act like brute beasts, enjoying the created world without ever recognizing or honoring the Creator who made it.

Evil people may multiply and succeed very quickly, like weeds sprouting overnight after rain. Their worldly success does not mean God is pleased with them. Their rapid rise only prepares the way for sudden, final destruction.

Earthly rebels rise only to fall, but the Lord remains exalted above all things forever. He reigns supreme on His throne in heaven, entirely untouched by human arrogance. His eternal majesty is the central truth that gives believers peace.

The repetition of the warning shows that the defeat of God's enemies is completely certain. Those who rebel against God cannot hold out against His power. In the end, all who commit evil will be scattered and brought to nothing.

While the wicked perish, God restores strength to His servant, pictured by the lifted horn of a strong wild ox. Pouring fresh, soothing oil over him represents the renewed joy, honor, and vitality that God provides. The believer can be confident that the Lord will sustain him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following ancient Greek and Latin versions, some read this phrase as God reviving a believer's failing strength and showing rich mercy in old age.

notes.meaning: The psalmist knows he will witness the downfall of those who set traps for him. Instead of seeking personal revenge, he calmly trusts God to defend the right. He leaves his enemies in the Lord's hands, confident that justice will be done.

The righteous are contrasted with the wicked, who wither like grass. Faithful believers resemble palm trees that stay green in the desert heat and bear sweet fruit, and Lebanon cedars that grow tall, solid, and last for centuries. God gives His people enduring strength and usefulness.

Believers flourish because they are rooted in God's presence and worship. Just like healthy trees sheltered in the courtyards of a palace or temple, those who live close to God receive life-giving spiritual strength every day.

Ordinary trees stop producing fruit when they get old, but the Lord keeps His servants fruitful to the very end of their lives. Even when physical vigor fades, older believers remain spiritually green and active. They bear the precious fruit of patience, wise counsel, and steady faith.

The lifelong fruitfulness of God's people is living proof that He keeps His word. The Lord is an unshakeable Rock who never fails those who rely on Him. Everything He does is fair, wise, and completely without fault.
